subject: Acme - post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Omar Lee <omar.lee@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Acme - post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan

Hi Priya / Omar,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Quick recap of the commitments from our side and a recommended shortlist tuned to your latency and factuality needs.

Recap of constraints: 95th percentile latency target ~350ms for short queries, sustained peak ~120 qps, high factuality on product/FAQ responses, and cost sensitivity on bulk routes.

High-level shortlist (initial):
- rw-fast-3B: Lowest latency, strong for short instructive prompts. Low per-token cost; small risk on long-context factuality.
- rw-accurate-13B: Highest factuality and multi-turn coherence, recommended for high-value routes and fallback. Higher latency/cost.
- rw-compact-3B-4bit: Quantized option for bulk inference; best cost savings, watch for entity recall regressions.

Attached is a short deck and our cost/latency CSV. Next step: with your approval we'll run the full prompt set in a us-west-2 sandbox and produce a short tradeoff report (quality, latency, estimated monthly run-rate).

Please confirm and I'll kick off provisioning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: acme-eval-deck-2026-02-25.pdf)
(Attachment: acme-cost-latency-estimates-20260225.csv)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>

Cc: Omar Lee <omar.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple of asks before you start the full run:
- Can you give the baseline 95th numbers for each candidate measured in us-west-2 (warm cache)? We need those to compare to our SLAs.
- Please include estimated monthly spend at 120 qps for each model (short-query profile: ~8 generated tokens avg).

Security: we require a SOC 2 summary and confirmation the sandbox does not persist PII. If you can include a short note on which telemetry is stored during the run, that helps our security review.

If those are ok, please start Phase 1.

 — Priya
Sr. Product Manager, Search & Assist  — Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Omar Lee <omar.lee@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan

Great questions — answers below and an expanded rationale for each candidate.

Latency (95p, warm cache, us-west-2 expected):
- rw-fast-3B: ~80-140ms
- rw-accurate-13B: ~220-380ms (heavily dependent on response length)
- rw-compact-3B-4bit: ~120-200ms

Estimated unit costs (approx at 120 qps sustained, 24/7; short queries avg 8 tokens generated):
- rw-fast-3B: ~$0.018 / 1k tokens -> est. $3.5k/month
- rw-accurate-13B: ~$0.085 / 1k tokens -> est. $16k/month
- rw-compact-3B-4bit: ~$0.006 / 1k tokens -> est. $1.2k/month

Quality tradeoffs and recommended routing:
- rw-fast-3B: Use as fast-path for low-complexity queries (search suggestions, short answers). Watch for occasional lapses with long, nested factual chains.
- rw-accurate-13B: Use as accurate-path for high-value, multi-turn support flows. Strongest at reducing hallucination and maintaining context.
- rw-compact-3B-4bit: Cost-efficient for bulk cheap responses; add a lightweight reranker (rw-fast-3B or rw-accurate-13B) to filter risky outputs.

Plan: If you sign off, we'll provision a 2-week sandbox in us-west-2 and run Phase 1 (full prompt set) + Phase 2 (synthetic peak). We'll provide a tradeoff report, per-prompt latency, token counts, example outputs, and a simple quality score from your rubric.

Rishi / Connor — can you confirm SOC2 summary link and sandbox ephemeral data policy?

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Omar Lee <omar.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan

Marissa —

Confirming: we can stand up a us-west-2 sandbox for a two-week eval. Key infra notes:
- Instance sizing: use the same instance classes we used in the demo; provision one cluster per candidate model.
- Data policy: sandbox will be ephemeral; logs contain request/response traces for debugging and latency metrics only. No PII will be persisted; any PII flagged during the run will be redacted by the runner script.
- SOC2: attaching the SOC2 summary link in the shared Drive (Drive: SOC2-summary-Redwood-2025.pdf) and I'll send the formal package to Priya via secure link.

Connor — please confirm autoscale policy and any quota checks.

-Rishi

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Omar Lee <omar.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan

All good from infra side. A few notes: 
- Autoscale: we'll use the policy from the deck (scale up at 60% CPU/queue depth). Canary ramp to 120 qps possible within 6 minutes.
- Quotas: no known quota constraints for us-west-2 but request an immediate heads-up if you need >200 qps across all candidates concurrently.
- ETA for Phase 1 results: 5 business days after provisioning.

Marissa — I'll start the sandbox provisioning once you confirm start time.

Connor
